correctness.rationale: For every vertex in part i, the open neighborhood is exactly the complement of that part, so its neighborhood sum is W-s_i. A -1 vertex in part i has a 2-neighbor exactly when some 2 lies outside that part. These are precisely the two STRD conditions. Multinomial choices then count all labelings with fixed part counts. Summing the neighborhood inequalities proves every feasible weight is at least two. Exhaustive adjacency-level verification through order eight agrees with both the criterion and every enumerator coefficient.

originality.rationale: The 2026 initiating complete-multipartite preprint explicitly advertises the signed total Roman domination number and domatic number, while targeted published-finding corpus and web searches found no all-function weight enumerator. The closest published-finding corpus record is the signed Roman, not signed total Roman, enumerator; closed-neighborhood versus open-neighborhood sums make the feasible systems non-equivalent. Full-text access to the 2026 preprint was unavailable in this run, which remains a documented residual risk rather than being treated as evidence of absence.

The invariant has active 2026 follow-up work, so concurrent enumerative work may not yet be indexed.

value.rationale: The result upgrades a freshly studied complete-multipartite scalar invariant to a complete distribution theorem. It identifies every feasible function by partwise counts and yields the exact number of STRD functions at every weight, including the number of minimum functions as a coefficient. This is natural reusable data for domatic-family searches and extremal questions, not a routine recomputation of the already published minimum.
